correctness.rationale: The centered Laurent expansion normalizes the density and its odd cosine pairings give the claimed first absolute moment. The shortest-translation bound is saturated by the half-circle indicator. For equality, the arc leakage function is strictly increasing up to half length, since the density is positive a.e.; in a canonical decomposition of a nontrivial finite-perimeter set every component would have to have half length, hence there is just one component. Coarea and nesting give the same half-circle at almost every nontrivial level. The antipodal kernel has constant term 1/(2 pi a) for odd n and first nonzero term (n/2)^(2q) u^(2q)/(2 pi a) for even n; integrating against 2(delta-u) gives exactly both orders, constants and remainders. For q=2 the center is n²+2 sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k² and the first moment after scaling x=n theta has an integrable O(|x|^-3) tail majorant. Two integrations by parts reduce the sinc moment to the cosine Frullani integral log 2. At arc lengths 0 and 2 pi the true quotient is undefined (the indicators are constant); L at those endpoints means its continuous extension by zero, as in the proof for proper arcs. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed. The independent finite script passed 60 antipodal deficit checks.
residual_risks: The deficit assertion is local on the one-arc family, not a stability estimate on the whole BV unit ball.
